drafted_from: tool:join-a-space's own row (its words, input schema, sample runs and steps) and what its sample runs answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Let a person join a shared space by the way its join rows allow: free, or by holding the access a row names", with {"space":"sample-club","subject":"ana@example.com"}. It runs tool:join-a-space and answers {"space":"sample-club","subject":"ana@example.com","joined":true,"state":"member","member_type":"member","how":"free"}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and keeps only its own rows (record:space, record:space-member, payment-event, record:commercial-offer, access-grant, access-effect-rule, effect-lifecycle) through the records door.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Let a person join a shared space by the way its join rows allow: free, or by holding the access a row names", and give it space (The space's id, the last part of its record:space row id); subject (The person, the way the space and your access rules name them).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:join-a-space and its input (the worked example shows one).
3. Read what comes back: Reads the space's record:space row and the person's record:space-member row.

4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: record:space (records:read); record:space-member (records:read, records:list, records:write); payment-event (records:list); record:commercial-offer (records:list); access-grant (records:list); access-effect-rule (records:list); effect-lifecycle (records:list).
